fields.label: condenser water
fields.description: A litre of clean water drawn out of dry air by the ancient condenser, in a stoppered flask. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: gorrask
fields.description: Legend on this rock says a stone-crab grew so vast and so old that it no longer fits inside any canyon it did not carve itself. Whatever the truth of that, a gorrask this big has never needed to hurry: it moves once, settles for a season, and the pool truce holds around it exactly as it holds around everything smaller. Its shell is old enough that whole weep-mat colonies have taken root along the seams. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: old gorrask
fields.description: The oldest gorrask there is, one to a world. A pump-and-lattice machine has grown into its shell over the ages and still runs, drawing water out of dry air. Wherever the crab settles for a season a pool wells up round it and the water truce holds; when it moves on the pool drains back. Cut the machine out and the crab dies, and so does the moving oasis. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: murrin
fields.description: A hand-length pool fish, deep-keeled, with one tall dorsal comb-fin that cuts the surface in rings whenever the pool is fed. The pools' rings-within-rings, alive. A silent pool with no murrin rings is the first sign an oasis is dying. The gentle baseline every stocked pool is measured against. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: skarrin
fields.description: A forearm-long pool fish that spends as much time above the water as in it. When the pool is fed a stocked pool boils with them, silver arcs snapping at the falling dew-smoke. It jumps, and it bites what it lands on — clears a pen wall from standing water; a handler leaning over the pool takes a face-strike. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: karrek
fields.description: Finger-length little armored fish, fin-rays hardened into serrated chitin combs. A boiling crowd that hits thrown feed like one animal and leaves nothing. Feed-throwing is safe; wading is not — a karrek swarm strips a bleeding cut white in seconds. Left hungry two days, the swarm starts on its own smallest. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: vizhik
fields.description: A wrist-thin eel, comb-gills fanned along the whole neck like a ruff, cold, quick, and never where you left it. When a pen is overfull, a vizhik pours itself out of the pen and crosses open rock on its gill-comb — into the next pool, the cistern, the water barrel, the kitchen stock-pot. Its bite is small and goes septic more often than it should. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: vhorrin
fields.description: The murrin silhouette scaled wrong — arm-long, dorsal comb ragged, deep-bodied. It IS a pool fish, the same stock, grown past the point where the pen can hold anything else. Any stocked pool left crowded and unculled grows one; the murrin rings thin week by week until one wide slow ring is doing all the surfacing. It takes fingers. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: loomu
fields.description: A cat-sized, boneless, dove-grey thing that hangs in the warm seep-throat water and repeats what it hears at the bank: the feed whistle, the wind through the vanes, a child's laugh, its keeper's name for it. Mild in the flesh, terrible in the ear — a loomu pen at night runs through its whole collection. Handlers stop teaching them words on purpose and cannot stop teaching them by accident. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: huldu
fields.description: A forearm-length velvet-skinned swimmer, dorsal comb folded flat like wet fur; clings when handled. Warm to the touch — not seep-warm, body-warm, with a pulse you can feel through the skin. Lifted from the water it does not thrash: it grips the handler's forearm and presses close, and it shivers. None whatsoever, which is its own kind of problem: the huldu is the row that makes the handler the uneasy party. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: ivvol
fields.description: A flat bottom-dweller, its comb a raised dorsal ridge set with a row of eyes — the ridge surfaces, the eyes count. A doormat-sized floor-thing that knows the feed schedule better than the apprentice does. Passive — but it learns. Pens with an ivvol have fewer vizhik escapes and no vhorrin has ever grown in one, and no farmer can tell you the mechanism. When finally netted it does not struggle; it goes still, and the whole ridge of eyes turns to the farmer, and it watches. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: sillik
fields.description: A palm-sized silver-grey licker that lives ON the vertical weep-faces themselves, spread flat against the rock, its whisker-comb fanned around the muzzle to comb the thin water film off the stone. Whole faces stipple with them wherever the rock runs wet. It harvests the thinnest water in the biome and never joins the crowd at the pool — the one native the water truce barely touches. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: mirrik
fields.description: Thumb-sized insects with water-combing mesh wings that mist-dance over the pools at dusk — from any distance, smoke rising off the water that flows the wrong way. It pollinates the blade-flora, and its cocoons are the source of dewsilk, the biome's signature trade good. The dusk swarm is the biome doing its actual living. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: ssurr
fields.description: A hound-sized reptile with one enormous half-circle crest-fan folded flat or blazing open — closed it is a blade, open it is a wheel. Its breeding displays happen at the pools, harmless and spectacular; the fan doubles as its dew-comb on the weeping faces, so courtship and drinking are the same gesture. The tamable charmer of the biome. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: tirbak
fields.description: A placid colossus, round-backed, with a row of dorsal rain-fins like a ship's ventilation cowls. It drinks once per wind-cycle and carries it for days, fins fanned to the wind as it walks — the caravan mount of the oasis string, and the beast the desert roads were beaded for. It replaces the muffalo/dromedary/elephant pack slot a donor mod once filled here. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: burrak
fields.description: A bear-sized wallower that digs catch-basins that outlive it — abandoned burrak digs are how new micro-oases start. A working oasis tolerates its one huge elder, worn claw-combs and all, the way a town tolerates its engineer; in fiction the biggest of them earns the name burradar, but it is the same animal grown vast, not a second kind. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: vhakk
fields.description: A long low courser with a single blade-crest running nape to tail like a dorsal keel — the margin made flesh. It never hunts at water, by design, not restraint; it drinks in strict rotation like everything else, and owns the approaches instead. Its patrol is the oasis's outermost wall, enforcing the geometry of pilgrimage that only exists here. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: vellak
fields.description: Camel-tall striders that walk the dry country between pools in single file down the caravan roads, dorsal sail-combs fanned to drink the wind as they come. From the rim, moving lines converging on water: pilgrimage made visible. The RM_ tier's own pilgrim ring — the free mod keeps the pilgrimage identity without a canon herd, which only stacks on top in the campaign. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: kirruk
fields.description: A hawk-sized soarer that rides the wind forced up the tall stone, long stiff wings that are themselves combs — slotted trailing edges like comb-teeth — hanging motionless on the updraft off a rock face, wings combing the wet air as it hangs. It drinks the way the biome does, on the wing, and lands only to nest on the rims. The RM_ tier's own sky presence. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: condenser water
fields.description: A litre of clean water drawn out of dry air by the ancient condenser, in a stoppered flask. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: dewsilk cocoon
fields.description: A damp, pearl-grey cocoon the size of a thumbnail, combed from the mesh wings of a tamed mirrik swarm. Spun at a tailor bench it becomes dewsilk. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: dewsilk
fields.description: A pale, weightless fabric spun from mirrik cocoons. It sheds water, stays cool against the skin and insulates well against heat; the Weeping Stones' one export that caravans ask for by name. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: murrin breeding stock

fields.label: murrin
fields.description: A hand-length pool fish, deep-keeled, one tall dorsal comb-fin still folding. Gentle in the net and gentle on the plate. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: skarrin
fields.description: A silver arc netted mid-air when the pool is fed — the one catch you make above the water. A missed net is a bite. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: karrek
fields.description: A basket-trapped handful of finger-length armored fish, chitin combs still snapping. Never a line, never bare hands. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: vizhik
fields.description: Picked off wet stone after an escape, gloved — not caught in the pool, caught traveling. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: loomu
fields.description: It came to the feed whistle. That IS the catch method, and everyone hates it. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: huldu
fields.description: Picked up. It holds on. The easiest catch on the farm, and the one that leaves the handler uneasy. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: ivvol
fields.description: Lifted from the floor at night, when the eye-ridge closes. By day it sees the net coming, every time. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: murrin-and-seep-salt broth
fields.description: The pilgrim's comfort dish: murrin simmered thin with a pinch of seep-salt. Nothing fancy — it tastes like the pool is well. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: karrek paste
fields.description: A basketful of karrek rendered at a stove into a dense, gray-brown ration. Caravan food for the oasis string — eaten with resignation, not enjoyment, but it does not spoil for a season. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: cull feast
fields.description: The set-piece dish of a working stocked pool: one culled vhorrin, dressed and served whole to the table that saved the farm for another season. Relief and unease in one dish — everyone eating it knows what it grew fat on. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: rendered huldu fat
fields.description: Fine cooking fat rendered from a huldu carcass — the best cooking on the planet, priced in exactly the discomfort of knowing what it came from. Any kitchen that knows what to do with it turns out a better dish for the addition. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: murrin meat
fields.description: Raw meat from a murrin, the stocked pool's gentle baseline. Good ordinary fish-flesh. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: skarrin meat
fields.description: Raw meat from a skarrin — the volume line, taken at real cost in face-strikes and torn nets. No doubt at all, which is why farmers keep stocking them despite everything. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: karrek meat
fields.description: Raw meat from a karrek swarm — individually nothing, rendered by the basketful into a rich paste that keeps (see: karrek paste). Doubt-free, handler-hostile to gather. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: vizhik meat
fields.description: Raw meat from a vizhik. Excellent eating, and the pens keep breeding them because they keep arriving on their own. The mild doubt is where it's been — nobody eats a vizhik pulled from the cistern without thinking about the cistern. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: vhorrin meat
fields.description: An enormous single harvest of rich flesh from a culled vhorrin. The doubt is arithmetic, not flavor: everyone at the feast knows what it grew fat on. See: the Cull Feast. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: loomu meat
fields.description: The tenderest meat in the biome, faintly sweet. It learned the whistle, and it answered the whistle, and it was netted with the whistle. Some farms keep one loomu only as the caller for the rest and swear they would never eat that one. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: huldu meat
fields.description: Rich and fatty, the winter-feast meat, renders a fine cooking fat (see: rendered huldu fat). It is warm, it clings, it has something like breath, and it was quiet all the way to the kitchen. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: ivvol meat
fields.description: Dense, mild, good keeping-meat. When finally netted it did not struggle — it went still, and the whole ridge of eyes turned to the farmer, and it watched. Eating the thing that ran your pool better than you did feels like eating the foreman. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: ikkal
fields.description: A palm-wide bladder that hangs at the surface with a comb of fringe trailing below it, sieving the dew-smoke out of the water as it falls. At dusk the whole pool is dimpled with them, tilted to the same side like cups set out. It has no fight in it; a child can lift one out. Thin eating, and nobody minds -- pilgrims cook them for the broth, which tastes faintly of the stones. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: tarrik
fields.description: A thumb-length shrimp-thing with antennae grown into two fine combs that it holds up into the current and licks clean. Kin to the mirrik above the water, and it shows: the same chitin, the same fringed silhouette, the same habit of mist-dancing at dusk, only underwater. It breeds in the shallows during the truce, in the open, in crowds -- which is why nobody who has sat at a pool at dusk can eat one without a small pang. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: duul
fields.description: A slow grey sock of a thing that lies on the pool floor and eats what settles -- silt, dung, dead dew-smoke, the ash blown in from the desert. A pool with duul in it stays clear; a pool without them clouds in a season. Every oasis keeper knows the count. It is edible in the sense that most things are. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: ullo
fields.description: A soft bell the size of two cupped hands, near-invisible by day, that lights a slow blue pulse from dusk. Ullo rise together and drift as a lit crowd while the fan-dancers display on the bank; the pools are places of romance and the ullo have never been told otherwise. Netted, it is a sting and a disappointment -- mostly water, a little meat, and the light goes out in your hands. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: ozhu
fields.description: A blind, comb-gilled eel that lives in the warm throat of the seep itself, down where the spring comes up through the stones. It surfaces at dusk to feed on the fallen dew-smoke and goes back down. Warm to the touch when landed, and it stays warm for a while, which unsettles people. The oldest pools have the longest ozhu; oasis-keepers claim they can taste which spring one came from. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: vobbal
fields.description: Eight soft arms and a bulb of a body, living in the hollows where the seep water enters the pool. It takes things. Pebbles, offerings, a dropped tool, a ring -- and it stacks them, carefully, in towers in the shallows, and knocks them down, and stacks them again. Some oases forbid catching them; most simply don't. The ones who do eat them say it is very good, in a voice that suggests they would rather not have. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: seep stone
fields.description: A smooth mineral concretion grown drop by drop in the spring throat itself, where the seep comes up through the stones -- the Weeping Stones in miniature, banded pale and dark the same way the cliffs above the pool are. Oasis-keepers set the best ones on the shrine at the water's edge; a lesser one is sold to a pilgrim as a keepsake of the truce. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: bladder-fruit
fields.description: A fat translucent pod cut from a bladderquill, sloshing with stored water and a little starchy pulp. Food and drink in one object -- where bladderquill stands, nobody dies thirsty. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: seep-salt
fields.description: Mineral-pale salt scraped from the rim of a steamfrond vent, tasting faintly of the underworld it rose from. A preservative and a spice; the only source of it on the planet is a working seep oasis. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: dewgourd
fields.description: A single melon-sized gourd, rind pale and waxy as the stone it grew in the shade of. Slow to grow, but a colony that has one crop under cultivation eats well for a long season -- the waxy rind keeps it edible long after most produce would have spoiled. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: dewblade
fields.description: Shin-high tufts of flat grey-green blades standing edge-on to the sun and face-on to the wind, each blade tipped with a drip-point that feeds its own root. Whole hillsides of them align like iron filings -- the wind made visible. The grass-analog and graze base of the biome, densest toward true water. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: weep-mat
fields.description: A dark green-black mat hugging the cold stone faces, ridged like corduroy, every ridge square to the sea-wind, glistening along the weep-lines. It grows exactly where the stone weeps, so a weep-mat is the wet black streak's green echo -- a face without one is a face that has gone dry. Graze for the sillik. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: verdimoss
fields.description: Cushions of blue-green moss growing in beaded lines along seep cracks -- and over the old machines, where it takes the colour of oxidised bronze. It marks the seep lines and ages the ruins: every relic in the biome is half-mossed, which is its own sacred ambiguity. Zero yield; pure register, cheap density. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: shadefern
fields.description: A deep-green fern growing only on the shaded face of standing stone, every frond swept to the cold side as if combed, its pale rachis catching what light bounces in. Marks which side of a rock is the cold side at a glance -- the stone-shade fern niche, now donor-free under its own name. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: bladderquill
fields.description: A knee-high fan of stiff translucent quills, each fat at the base with stored water, standing in arcs along the green ring. Cut a quill and it sloshes. It bears the bladder-fruit -- food and drink in one object -- and is the visible promise of the green ring: where bladderquill stands, nobody dies thirsty. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: salvecomb
fields.description: One waist-high arched frond per plant, serrated along its windward edge like a comb's teeth, silver-downy where it combs the fog. Grows alone in shade lines. Its down mats wick clean condensate; field dressing is the fiction. Rare enough to be worth a walk under the overhangs. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: rockfinger
fields.description: A gnarled, wind-stripped hardwood rooted in the rim cracks of the tall stone, branches clawing out over the drop, bark pale as the stone it grips. At this biome's low sun its shadow runs down the rock face and across the ground for many times its height -- you meet the shadow before the tree. Scarce, and hardy the way it has to be. Slow, scattered, precious timber in high stone country; a felled rockfinger is a caravan event. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: dripfringe
fields.description: A curtain of dark fleshy fingers hanging from overhang lips and cistern mouths, each finger a drip-tip, forever ticking water into the catch-pool below. The comb inverted -- teeth down. A dripfringe curtain over a dark mouth means water below. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: steamfrond
fields.description: A rosette of mineral-pale fronds spiralled around a breathing vent, rims crusted with white salt bloom. Grows only at the seep oases -- the green eye in open nothing is a steamfrond ring before it is anything else. Its harvest scrapes seep-salt, a preservative and spice with the underworld's taste, and the only source of it. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: dewgourd
fields.description: Owner's spec, verbatim: "a large melon like gourd that takes a long time to grow but is then worth a lot of food and keeps for a long time." A single melon-sized gourd per plant, rind pale and waxy as the stone, swelling in the shade of its own little blade-comb, fed by drip. One slow gourd is a season's promise -- the reason a colony can farm here. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: spin dewsilk
fields.description: Spin mirrik cocoons into dewsilk fabric. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: cook pool-fry basket
fields.description: Cook a simple basket of skarrin and karrek — the stocked farm's daily bread. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: cook murrin-and-seep-salt broth
fields.description: Simmer murrin thin with a pinch of seep-salt — the taste of the stones. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: render karrek paste

fields.label: cook the cull feast

fields.label: render huldu fat
fields.description: Render a huldu carcass into fine cooking fat — the best cooking on the planet, priced in the discomfort. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: the Weeping Stones
fields.description: High pale stone standing in the path of the sea-wind. Most of this country is bright, dry, wind-scoured ridge and shoulder -- but every cold shaded face of it weeps: thin black streaks of wet running down white rock, moss crowding the seep lines, and here and there a true pool with a green ring around it and a crowd at the water. An oasis here is never merely found water; it is a working thing, part stone, part machine, part congregation of everything that drinks. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: ancient condenser plant
fields.description: A pump-and-lattice machine the size of a wardrobe, cut whole from the shell of the oldest gorrask. It still draws water out of dry air, slowly, without power or fuel. It is the last one that works. Carry it, install it on a ship, and it will keep on weeping into whatever you set under it. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: old gorrask
fields.description: The oldest gorrask there is, one to a world. A pump-and-lattice machine has grown into its shell over the ages and still runs, drawing water out of dry air. Wherever the crab settles for a season a pool wells up round it and the water truce holds; when it moves on the pool drains back. Cut the machine out and the crab dies, and so does the moving oasis. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes
